text:
anya: heads-up: canary for Nereid-14b (int4) is showing warm-start OOMs on long gens (>1200 tokens). fragmentation metric shoots up after first heavy request and stays elevated.
deploy-bot: Canary deployed nereid-14b-int4 @ pool-gamma (12 replicas).
leo: can you share repro steps + GPU type? microbatch config?
anya: single-stream chat, target 1200-1500 tokens, seen on A100 and H100, microbatch=1 reproduces fastest.
ciara: likely KV-slot churn + allocator free-list fragmentation. int4 reduces memory but increases allocation boundaries. similar pattern to previous 14b cases.
ben: log excerpt at OOM:
```
[E] cudaMalloc failed: OutOfMemory
requested=1.18GiB for attn_kv
allocator post-oom: free_chunks=12, largest_free=64MiB
heap_trend: 2.3GiB -> 1.8GiB -> 420MiB
```
leo: low-risk mitigations: lower default max_new_tokens 1024 -> 512, disable prefetch on warm path, enable slab_compact_on_eviction, add a small startup-prime generation (80-120 tokens) to stabilize KV shapes.
ciara: also keep microbatch small for latency but add a 20ms batching window and allow max_concurrent=2 to consolidate bursts and reduce churn.
ben: I'll run an A/B overnight comparing baseline vs frag-mit (collecting alloc histograms, free-chunk counts, per-replica OOMs every 5m).
Command:
```
./canary_runner --model nereid-14b --quant int4 \
  --baseline "max_new=1024,prefetch=true,kv_thresh=0.8,slab_compact=false" \
  --variant  "max_new=512,prefetch=false,kv_thresh=0.6,slab_compact=true,startup_prime=true" \
  --workload long-gen --duration 8h --collect alloc_hist:5m --collect frag_metrics:5m
```
anya: include conv-bench 1k prompts quality check (Rouge/LLMScore) for regressions.
leo: capture traces on any OOM, latency p95, and token-rate.
ciara: rollout plan if variant OK: canary -> 30% (24h) -> 60% (24h) -> 100% with FP16 fallback if OOM rate > 0.5% or P95 latency regresses > 20%.
ben: starting run now, will post summary + charts tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:
